question: how many compressed bytes a page is once the markup shared across a site is counted once, and what the unique part and a node record weigh
instrument: plain HTTPS GETs, then Node zlib gzip, brotli and zstd (zstd with a raw dictionary for the RFC 9842 case)

method.pages per site: home plus up to 20 internal links
method.page choice: links from the home page without query strings, pages with a known JSON:API alias first, the rest spread evenly
method.shell: lines common to the fetched pages: the median-length page cut down by each other page in turn (longest common subsequence); a page that would cut the shell below 60% of its length is an outlier, left out of the shell and counted whole as its unique part
method.unique part: the page lines outside the shell, with an @n line for each run of n shell lines
method.dictionary: zstd raw dictionary of up to 4 other pages of the site, capped at 1048576 B
method.json rendered: title, dates, alias, body and non-empty field_* attributes; references excluded
method.json pairing: a node pairs with a page when its path alias equals the page path; other nodes go to nodeSample
method.sizes unit: bytes; gzip 6 and 9, brotli 5 and 11, zstd 3 and 19

exclusions: https://www.berkeley.edu/: no Drupal markup in the home page
https://www.cornell.edu/: no Drupal markup in the home page
https://www.georgetown.edu/: no Drupal markup in the home page
https://www.harvard.edu/: no Drupal markup in the home page
